title: In Praise of Folly
subtitle: A tiny boat adrift upon a sea of ideals, convinced it has hoisted its sail.

content.text: Look, it's sinking. Corpses float on the planks, and the fleeing prisoners are swimming toward the shore. Time to abandon ship.

branch.text: One that was exiled to a desolate corner of the ocean by the resplendent civilized world.
It's both a prison and a sanitarium. Are any of your friends aboard? If so, you might find the following report a little offensive.
"Dregs of society" ... "Human scum" ... These are the terms used to describe its eccentric passengers.
To be fair, they do lack discipline and independence.
But that may well be a response to the heavy pain they've endured.
Some theorists suggest that they're innocent victims, trapped in the confines between rationality and irrationality, defined and redefined by historians as they please.
But let's ditch the theories and simplify things: the moment the shackle called "madness" was fastened around their necks—whether they were truly mentally ill or not—their lives were forever scarred.
And now, the mad passengers are storming the shore.
I suppose it is. You can see the joy in their faces, even in the footprints they leave behind as they hop across the beach.
Yes, freedom is favorable, indeed. The freedom to squander our lives, to trample on the dignity of others, the freedom to embrace absurdity and meaninglessness.
But one can gain immunity through controlled infection—the disease can become its own vaccine.
Just beware of the ignorant commander who deifies a wandering lunatic in pursuit of a little knowledge.
Let's dig deeper—scavenge through the messy battlefield for dog tags—were these people born mad?
After watching the inhabitants of this earth tear each other apart in one war after another, I've concluded this: only knowledge drives people to madness; ignorance does not.
Madness is a side effect of the sedative that is "knowledge." As long as those on land continue to consume it, this ship will never be short on recruits.
This is a war between madness and civilization. Both sides have leveled accusations, spilled blood, and pummeled each other ...
... and soon, everyone will have leapt into the trenches and beaten and been beaten to a bloody pulp. Only a few can escape this fate.
Like who?
Check your six.
The one leaning against the sunken ship, showing no signs of struggle or sorrow—García.
The seawater has flooded his windpipe and reddened his eyes, yet there he is, staring blankly at the shore ...
He's in his home base. He holds no hope for forgiveness from his enemies—not in the slightest. He's a one-man army, fighting only for himself. Alone.
Now, do a 360 and look again—he's been utterly defeated.

items.text: In Praise of Folly
A prisoner steps out from behind the wall, a weapon held in his shaking hand.

items.speaker: García
items.text: I was just setting up my exhibit when everything started shaking. Then I realized it wasn't just my imagination.

items.speaker: García
items.text: So I followed the cracks in the wall and found my way here.

items.speaker: García
items.text: I didn't mean to eavesdrop, but something's happening to the Panopticon, isn't it?
His panicked hands shift the gun toward Aleph, who has collapsed on his side.

items.speaker: García
items.text: Are you the Physician? Or is it Aleph?

items.speaker: García
items.text: Whoever you are, please, please restore the Panopticon to the way it was! I'm begging you!

items.speaker: García
items.text: You-You can do that, right?
The mind that once created infinity now watches as it folds back into nothing before him.

items.speaker: García
items.text: Why? Why aren't you doing anything? Damn it! Why is this happening?

items.speaker: García
items.text: Oh, oh, the die! If you won't help me, then I'll do it myself!
The prisoner, in desperation, lunges forward.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Calm down, García!

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Timekeeper, he's ...
García, weakened by his long confinement, is easily knocked to the ground, unable to withstand even the lightest touch of arcane skill.

items.speaker: García
items.text: Why? Why is this happening to me?

items.speaker: García
items.text: I was so close ... so close to completing the exhibition.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Can't you see, García? There is no one controlling this place now! You're free!

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: It isn't the die that's trapped you, nor is it the walls of this prison.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: It's the rules and that overpowering gaze from the central tower, but now that's all gone.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: You can go outside. You can set up your exhibit anywhere you want. No need to stay stuck in this—
Looking back on all that he has lost, the artist cuts her off.

items.speaker: García
items.text: No, Ms. Recoleta. You've seen the world out there. You know as well as I ...

items.speaker: García
items.text: ... that there's nowhere else I can go but here.

items.speaker: García
items.text: This is the only place in the world where I can hold my exhibit.

items.speaker: García
items.text: And you've ruined it. You've ruined everything.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: This room's about to collapse. We've got to leave.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Mr. García, do you need a hand?

items.speaker: García
items.text: I can take care of myself, thank you.

items.speaker: García
items.text: I ... I'll go a different way. I have to go back and finish setting up my exhibit.
He drags himself forward with trudging steps, retracing his path to leave.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Vertin, what about Aleph? We can't just leave him here.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Of course not. We still have questions he needs to answer.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Sonetto, help me get him up. Let's get out of here.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Yes, Timekeeper.
The dejected prisoner looks at Sonetto with confusion.

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: Your words are always at odds with your thoughts. You carry an ocean of questions, yet never reveal even a single drop of them.

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: Why have you never shared your doubts? Why do you stay silent in the face of everything and everyone around you?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: I ... I believe in my duty.
The prisoner shifts his gaze to the other Foundation investigator.

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: As for you, Paracausality Researcher. You're different from any other seeker of answers.

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: Even on a desperate, near hopeless journey, your heart holds little doubt.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Perhaps not every question needs an answer, Mr. Aleph.

items.speaker: Aleph
items.text: Is that so?
The prisoner, so used to answering others' questions, seems to have run into one of his own. But unfortunately, no one is here to answer it.
